name: Congenital Genu Recurvatum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Genu Recurvatum

criteria.description: Visible hyperextension of the knee joint beyond normal physiological limits at birth
Radiographic evidence of posterior tibial slope alteration and knee joint hyperextension
No history of trauma or acquired causes explaining knee hyperextension
Presence of associated congenital musculoskeletal deformities such as foot deformities or ligamentous laxity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical hyperextension at birth and radiographic confirmation of genu recurvatum without acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; exclusion of acquired causes is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Knee joint hyperextension exceeding 15 degrees at birth
searchTerms: knee bends backward over 15 degrees at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Posterior tibial slope flattening or reversal on imaging
searchTerms: flattened or reversed slope of shin bone on x-ray
posterior tibial slope abnormality on imaging

common.symptomName: Ligamentous laxity around the knee joint
Gait abnormalities including hyperextended stance phase
searchTerms: abnormal gait with stiff knee stance

common.symptomName: Associated foot deformities such as clubfoot
Muscle weakness around the knee extensors
searchTerms: weak thigh muscles that straighten knee

occasional.symptomName: Mild anterior knee pain during activity
searchTerms: mild front knee pain with activity
slight pain in kneecap when moving

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones due to lower limb deformity
searchTerms: late motor skills due to leg deformity

rare.symptomName: Secondary osteoarthritis of the knee in adolescence
searchTerms: early arthritis in knee during adolescence

rare.symptomName: Neurovascular compromise due to severe deformity
searchTerms: nerve and blood flow problems from severe deformity
circulation and nerve issues due to limb deformity

rare.symptomName: Skin breakdown over anterior knee due to hyperextension
searchTerms: ulceration due to knee bending backward

imaging: Lateral knee radiographs showing hyperextension and posterior tibial slope alteration
MRI to assess ligamentous integrity and soft tissue structures
genetic: No specific gene identified; may be associated with connective tissue disorders in some cases
other: Physical examination demonstrating hyperextension and ligamentous laxity

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma or neuromuscular disease
Radiographic evidence of growth plate injury or deformity
Multiple joint contractures rather than hyperextension

redFlags: Rapid progression of knee hyperextension deformity
Neurovascular symptoms such as numbness or decreased pulses
Skin ulceration or breakdown over the knee joint
references: Smith et al. (2018). Congenital Genu Recurvatum: Clinical Features and Management. Journal of Pediatric Orthopedics.
Jones and Patel (2020). Imaging Characteristics of Congenital Knee Deformities. Radiology Clinics.
